title: Hyatt Vendor Facts
skill:
# Hyatt — Vendor Facts (citation-backed reference)

> Static, citation-stable reference of **Hyatt's own facts** — portfolio scale, the brand
> families relevant to corporate accounts, the Hyatt Leverage business-travel program,
> World of Hyatt, meetings & events capabilities, and the 1957 heritage and purpose
> statement. These do **not** change from one target account to another, so an ABM page
> builder should pull them from here rather than re-researching them every run. Scope is
> **Hyatt corporate / enterprise B2B only** — group room blocks, meeting & event space, and
> year-round business travel. Sources are **hyatt.com**, **hyatt.com/leverage** and
> **world.hyatt.com**, retrieved 2026-08-10; each fact carries its source in the Sources list.
>
> **Concept-demonstration notice:** this file was authored for an Optimizely Opal POC and
> for account-based-marketing training. It is **not** an official communication of Hyatt
> Hotels Corporation, and pages built from it must carry the same disclaimer in their footer.
>
> **Integrity rule:** treat this file as the allow-list of Hyatt figures. Do not add a Hyatt
> statistic, award, program benefit, or property claim that is not on this list. If a page
> needs a Hyatt fact that isn't here, state the **qualitative** claim or mark it unavailable
> — never estimate a number. Customer names, awards and outcome statistics are **not** on
> this list and must not be invented.

Hyatt Hotels Corporation is a global hospitality company operating and franchising hotels,
resorts and residences, and selling to corporate and enterprise accounts across three
commercial pillars: group room blocks, meeting & event space, and the Hyatt Leverage
business-travel program.

---

## Purpose & heritage

- Hyatt's stated purpose: **"We care for people so they can be their best."** [S1]
- Hyatt has been caring for guests **since 1957**, when the first hotel opened. [S1]

## Portfolio scale (the only scale figures a page may cite)

- **1,500+ hotels and resorts** worldwide. [S1]
- Present in **83 countries across six continents**. [S1]

> Cite these two figures as-is. If a page wants a more granular breakdown (rooms, pipeline,
> per-region counts), that figure is **not** in this file — use the qualitative claim
> ("a global portfolio") instead.

## Brand families relevant to corporate accounts

- **Hyatt Regency** — the connected convention and meetings brand; large function space,
  the natural default for a group block around a conference. [S2]
- **Grand Hyatt** — large-scale flagship hotels in major gateway cities, sized for whole
  delegations. [S2]
- **Andaz** — locally inspired boutique hotels; character space for creative sessions and
  smaller executive gatherings. [S2]
- **Hyatt Place** — efficient select-service hotels, well suited to crew, staff and
  cost-managed delegate rooms. [S2]
- **Hyatt House** — extended-stay hotels with kitchens and residential suites, for
  instructors, crews and longer training tours. [S2]
- **The Unbound Collection by Hyatt** — independent, one-of-a-kind properties for
  distinctive receptions and closing-night events. [S2]

> Use the brand names exactly as written above. Individual property names, distances and
> function-space capacities are **account research**, not vendor facts — verify each
> property on hyatt.com and cite it under group `"account"` with a qualified distance
> ("~10 min walk"), never as an unqualified claim.

## Meetings & events capabilities

- Hyatt sells **meetings and events** to organisations, covering group room blocks,
  meeting and event space, and event catering, with a Hyatt sales contact per property or
  region. [S3]
- Supported meeting formats commonly available across the meetings-oriented brands include
  **classroom, boardroom, theatre/cabaret and workshop setups**, event catering, and
  **hybrid-capable A/V and event internet**. [S3]

> Room counts, ceiling heights, square footage and specific A/V inventory vary by property
> and are **not** in this file. Describe the capability, then point the reader at a proposal.

## Hyatt Leverage (corporate / business-travel program)

- **Hyatt Leverage** is Hyatt's business-travel program for companies, offering negotiated
  discounts for a company's travellers. [S4]
- Savings are **up to approximately 15% off standard rates** at participating hotels
  worldwide. [S4]
- The program provides an **online admin experience** for enrolling a company and managing
  its travel program (bookings, spend and travellers). [S4]
- **World of Hyatt** points and elite-night credit are still earned by travellers on
  qualifying stays booked through the program. [S4][S5]
- Eligibility, participating hotels, and benefits are subject to program terms — always
  render "up to ~15%" with the "terms and eligibility apply" qualifier. [S4]

## World of Hyatt (loyalty)

- **World of Hyatt** is Hyatt's loyalty program; members earn **points and elite night
  credit on qualifying stays** and redeem points for free nights. [S5]
- For a corporate account, the useful framing is that individual travellers keep earning
  personally while the company banks the negotiated rate. [S4][S5]

## Known caveats / do-not-conflate

- **No customer names, no outcome statistics, no awards.** None are included here. Do not
  cite a Hyatt client, case study, satisfaction score, or industry award on a page built
  from this file.
- **"Up to ~15%" is a ceiling, not an entitlement.** Never restate it as "15% savings" or
  "save 15%". Keep "up to" and keep the terms qualifier.
- **Property-level claims are account research.** Hotel names, walking distances, capacity
  and availability change; they belong under source group `"account"` with a live hyatt.com
  citation, not under `"hyatt"`.
- **Playful or illustrative figures are allowed only when labelled.** The experiment/A-B
  section of a proposal page may use directional, obviously-illustrative numbers, but it
  **must** carry a visible footnote saying they are estimates — they are never sourced here.
- **Brand availability varies by market.** Every brand listed above is a real Hyatt brand,
  but a given city may not have one — confirm on hyatt.com before naming a brand in a
  city-specific shortlist.

## How the page builder uses this file

1. Pull every Hyatt-side fact from this file instead of re-researching hyatt.com per run.
2. Emit each fact used as an entry in the page's `sources` array with group **`"hyatt"`**,
   reusing the label, URL and publisher from the Sources list below. Research on the
   prospect uses group **`"account"`**.
3. Reference the source inline with a `[^n]` marker wherever the claim appears, matching the
   `n` of the `sources` entry.
4. If a needed Hyatt fact is absent, write the qualitative claim and add no source — do not
   fabricate a figure to fill the gap.

---

## Sources (retrieved 2026-08-10)

- [S1] About Hyatt — purpose, heritage and portfolio scale — Hyatt — https://www.hyatt.com/about-hyatt — retrieved 2026-08-10
- [S2] Hyatt Brands — Hyatt — https://www.hyatt.com/brands — retrieved 2026-08-10
- [S3] Meetings & Events — Hyatt — https://www.hyatt.com/meetings-and-events — retrieved 2026-08-10
- [S4] Hyatt Leverage — business travel program — Hyatt — https://www.hyatt.com/leverage — retrieved 2026-08-10
- [S5] World of Hyatt — https://world.hyatt.com — retrieved 2026-08-10
skill_sementics: Static, citation-backed reference of Hyatt's own corporate/enterprise B2B facts: purpose ("We care for people so they can be their best") and 1957 heritage; portfolio scale (1,500+ hotels and resorts, 83 countries across six continents); the brand families relevant to corporate accounts (Hyatt Regency, Grand Hyatt, Andaz, Hyatt Place, Hyatt House, The Unbound Collection by Hyatt); meetings & events capabilities (group room blocks, meeting and event space, classroom/boardroom/theatre setups, catering, hybrid-capable A/V); the Hyatt Leverage business-travel program (negotiated corporate rates with savings of up to ~15% off standard rates, admin dashboard, terms apply); and World of Hyatt (points and elite night credit on qualifying stays). Customer names, outcome statistics and awards are deliberately excluded and must not be invented. Use when building or editing any Hyatt ABM / account proposal / persona page so vendor facts come from a verified Hyatt source instead of being re-researched or invented; emit each fact into the page's sources array with group "hyatt" (prospect research uses group "account"). All figures sourced from hyatt.com, hyatt.com/leverage and world.hyatt.com. Concept-demonstration asset for ABM training — not an official Hyatt communication.
